Downstream analysis on scRNA-seq from mouse spermatogenesis using SCALPEL

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Seurat, quietly = TRUE))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr, quietly = TRUE))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table, quietly = TRUE))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(scalpelR, quietly = TRUE))
Note

Note: Install scalpelR for downstream analysis

The functions used in this downstream analysis are provided by the R package scalpelR, installed from its Github page:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Franzx7/scalpelR@dev")
library(scalpelR)
Function Use
FindIsoforms Differential isoform usage between groups of cells (same method as the pipeline DIU table).
plotUsage Isoform usage (fraction of the gene) per group and sample.
CoveragePlot Read coverage of a gene per group of cells, from the SCALPEL filtered BAM files.
weightedUTR_cell Weighted 3’ UTR length per cell.
subsetBAM BAM file of the reads of selected cells (e.g. genome browser).

1 Introduction

In this example, we perform a gene and isoform level single-cell analysis of the 10X 3’ Chromium scRNA-seq dataset of adult mouse spermatogenesis (GSE104556, samples SRR6129050 and SRR6129051, two mice), processed with Cell Ranger (mm10-2020-A reference) and SCALPEL with the default parameters, on the full dataset:

nextflow run plasslab/nf-core-scalpel -r dev -profile singularity \
    --samplesheet samplesheet.csv \
    --transcriptome gencode.vM23.transcripts.fa.gz \
    --gtf gencode.vM23.annotation.gtf.gz \
    --genome GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz \
    --outdir results

The files used by this downstream analysis are:

> tree results/differential results/filtered_bams results/isoform -L 1
results/differential
├── DIU_table.csv
├── DIU_warnings.txt
├── iDGE_seurat.RDS
└── samples_qc.tsv
results/filtered_bams
├── SRR6129050_filtered.bam
├── SRR6129050_filtered.bam.bai
├── SRR6129051_filtered.bam
└── SRR6129051_filtered.bam.bai
results/isoform
├── chr1.annots.gz
...

2 Gene-level analysis: cell types

We first annotate the cells with a standard gene-level analysis of the Cell Ranger count matrices. Low-quality cells (less than 1000 detected genes or more than 10% of mitochondrial reads, ~35% of the Cell Ranger cells) are discarded: they blur the isoform-level analysis even more than the gene-level one, as their few UMIs are split between the isoforms of each gene. The cell types are then annotated with marker genes of the spermatogenesis stages (spermatocytes, round spermatids, elongating spermatids) and of the somatic cells.

#- Cell Ranger gene counts of the two samples...
dge.obj = lapply(c("SRR6129050", "SRR6129051"), function(s){
    o = CreateSeuratObject(Read10X(file.path("cellranger", s, "outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix")), project = s)
    o$orig.ident = s
    o$Barcodes = colnames(o)
    o
})
dge.obj = merge(dge.obj[[1]], dge.obj[[2]], add.cell.ids = c("SRR6129050", "SRR6129051")) %>% JoinLayers()

#- quality control: >= 1000 genes & < 10% mitochondrial reads...
dge.obj[["percent.mt"]] = PercentageFeatureSet(dge.obj, pattern = "^mt-")
VlnPlot(dge.obj, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"), group.by = "orig.ident", pt.size = 0, log = T)
dge.obj = subset(dge.obj, subset = nFeature_RNA >= 1000 & percent.mt < 10)

dge.obj = dge.obj %>% NormalizeData(verbose = F) %>% FindVariableFeatures(nfeatures = 3000, verbose = F) %>%
    ScaleData(verbose = F) %>% RunPCA(npcs = 30, verbose = F) %>% FindNeighbors(dims = 1:20, verbose = F) %>%
    FindClusters(resolution = 0.5, verbose = F) %>% RunUMAP(dims = 1:20, verbose = F)

#- cell type of each cluster: highest (scaled) marker score...
markers = list(
    "spermatocytes" = c("Sycp3", "Piwil1", "Hormad1", "Spo11", "Ccna1", "Pttg1"),
    "round spermatids" = c("Acrv1", "Spaca1", "Tex36", "Lyar", "Sun5", "Hemgn"),
    "elongating spermatids" = c("Prm1", "Prm2", "Tnp1", "Tnp2", "Oaz3", "Gsg1"),
    "somatic" = c("Sox9", "Amh", "Insl3", "Cyp17a1", "Vim", "Acta2"))
dge.obj = AddModuleScore(dge.obj, features = markers, name = "score")
scores = scale(as.matrix(dge.obj[[]][, paste0("score", seq_along(markers))]))
cl = aggregate(scores, by = list(cluster = dge.obj$seurat_clusters), FUN = mean)
dge.obj$celltype = names(markers)[apply(cl[, -1], 1, which.max)][match(dge.obj$seurat_clusters, cl$cluster)]
table(dge.obj$orig.ident, dge.obj$celltype)
            
             elongating spermatids round spermatids somatic spermatocytes
  SRR6129050                  1185             1260      59          1320
  SRR6129051                  1013             1436      81          1059

3 Downstream analysis of SCALPEL results

3.1 Loading the isoform-based Seurat object

The isoform-based Seurat object generated by SCALPEL has one counts layer per sample and cells named <sample>_<barcode> (as the gene-level object above). We keep the cells passing the gene-level quality control:

idge.obj = readRDS("results/differential/iDGE_seurat.RDS")
#- counts are stored in one layer per sample (Seurat v5): join them
idge.obj = JoinLayers(idge.obj)
#- cells passing the quality control & their cell types from the gene-level analysis...
idge.obj = subset(idge.obj, cells = intersect(colnames(idge.obj), colnames(dge.obj)[dge.obj$celltype != "somatic"]))
idge.obj$celltype = dge.obj$celltype[match(colnames(idge.obj), colnames(dge.obj))]
idge.obj
An object of class Seurat 
76196 features across 7273 samples within 1 assay 
Active assay: RNA (76196 features, 0 variable features)
 1 layer present: counts

3.2 Dimensionality reduction and clustering

The isoform quantification can be used as a gene-level count matrix. Isoforms detected in less than 10 cells are discarded:

idge.obj = subset(idge.obj, features = rownames(idge.obj)[Matrix::rowSums(LayerData(idge.obj, layer = "counts") > 0) >= 10])
#- as isoform data is more sparse, we use a higher number of variable features
idge.obj = idge.obj %>% NormalizeData(verbose = F) %>% FindVariableFeatures(nfeatures = 6000, verbose = F) %>%
    ScaleData(verbose = F) %>% RunPCA(npcs = 30, verbose = F) %>% RunUMAP(dims = 1:20, verbose = F)
DimPlot(idge.obj, group.by = "celltype", label = T, repel = T, pt.size = .5, label.size = 5) %>%
    theme_umap() + ggtitle("iDGE-based UMAP")

3.3 Differential isoform usage

scalpelR::FindIsoforms tests the differential isoform usage between groups of cells with the same method as the pipeline (differential/DIU_table.csv, obtained directly with --clusters). With more than 2 groups, each group is compared with the rest. We use the permutation test (cells permuted between the groups within each sample) and the SCALPEL isoform annotation (3’ ends):

diu.table = FindIsoforms(
    seurat_obj = idge.obj,
    group_by = "celltype",
    sample_by = "orig.ident",
    isoform_annotation = "results/isoform",
    test = "permutation",
    cores = 8)
#- genes with a differential isoform usage per comparison...
diu.table %>% distinct(comparison, gene_name, event_type, direction) %>% count(comparison, event_type, direction)
                      comparison                event_type   direction     n
                          <char>                    <char>      <char> <int>
1: elongating spermatids_vs_rest alternative_terminal_exon        <NA>   884
2: elongating spermatids_vs_rest               tandem_3UTR lengthening    85
3: elongating spermatids_vs_rest               tandem_3UTR  shortening   322
4:      round spermatids_vs_rest alternative_terminal_exon        <NA>  1390
5:      round spermatids_vs_rest               tandem_3UTR lengthening   148
6:      round spermatids_vs_rest               tandem_3UTR  shortening   318
7:         spermatocytes_vs_rest alternative_terminal_exon        <NA>  1620
8:         spermatocytes_vs_rest               tandem_3UTR lengthening   483
9:         spermatocytes_vs_rest               tandem_3UTR  shortening   104

The table has one row per isoform (genes with a differential isoform usage: adjusted p-value < 0.05, usage change >= 0.1, change in the same direction in both mice):

diu.table %>% filter(comparison == "round spermatids_vs_rest") %>%
    select(gene_name, transcript_name, event_type, direction, delta_3end, counts.group1, counts.group2, PU.group1, PU.group2,
           delta_PU, p.value.adjusted, replicated, delta_PU_by_sample) %>%
    mutate(p.value.adjusted = format(p.value.adjusted, digits = 2)) %>%
    head(10) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 3)

The tandem 3’ UTR events (isoforms sharing their terminal exon) give the direction of the 3’ UTR changes: shorter 3’ UTRs in round and elongating spermatids, longer 3’ UTRs in spermatocytes, as described for the global 3’ UTR shortening during spermatogenesis:

diu.table %>% filter(event_type == "tandem_3UTR") %>% distinct(comparison, gene_name, direction) %>%
    ggplot(aes(sub("_vs_rest", "", comparison), fill = direction)) + geom_bar(position = "fill", color = "black", linewidth = .2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(lengthening = "#1b9e77", shortening = "#d95f02")) +
    xlab(NULL) + ylab("fraction of tandem 3' UTR genes") + ggtitle("3' UTR changes vs the other cell types") +
    coord_flip() + theme_bw(base_size = 12)

3.4 Isoform usage of a gene

For example, the gene Reep1 uses its proximal 3’ end (Reep1-202) in round spermatids and its distal 3’ end (Reep1-201) in the other cells, in both mice:

diu.table %>% filter(gene_name == "Reep1", comparison == "round spermatids_vs_rest") %>%
    select(transcript_name, event_type, direction, delta_3end, counts.group1, counts.group2, PU.group1, PU.group2, delta_PU, dist_3end, p.value.adjusted, replicated, delta_PU_by_sample) %>%
    mutate(p.value.adjusted = format(p.value.adjusted, digits = 2)) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 3)
transcript_name event_type direction delta_3end counts.group1 counts.group2 PU.group1 PU.group2 delta_PU dist_3end p.value.adjusted replicated delta_PU_by_sample 
plotUsage(idge.obj, gene_in = "Reep1", group_by = "celltype", sample_by = "orig.ident", isoform_annotation = "results/isoform",
    groups = c("spermatocytes", "round spermatids", "elongating spermatids"))

The isoform expression can also be visualized on the UMAP:

FeaturePlot(idge.obj, features = c("Reep1***Reep1-202", "Reep1***Reep1-201"), order = T, pt.size = .5, cols = c("gray85", "red"))

3.5 Read coverage

scalpelR::CoveragePlot plots the coverage of the reads used by SCALPEL (filtered_bams) for each group of cells, normalized by the number of cells, with the structure of the isoforms (thick: CDS, thin: UTR):

gtf = rtracklayer::import("refs/gencode.vM23.annotation.gtf.gz")
bams = c(SRR6129050 = "results/filtered_bams/SRR6129050_filtered.bam", SRR6129051 = "results/filtered_bams/SRR6129051_filtered.bam")
CoveragePlot(idge.obj, bamfiles = bams, gene_in = "Reep1", genome_gr = gtf, group_by = "celltype",
    groups = c("spermatocytes", "round spermatids", "elongating spermatids"), distZOOM = 3500, extend = 500)

Isoform switches between alternative terminal exons are also detected, e.g. Zfhx3 (no 3’ UTR direction: the isoforms end in different exons):

plotUsage(idge.obj, gene_in = "Zfhx3", group_by = "celltype", sample_by = "orig.ident", isoform_annotation = "results/isoform",
    groups = c("spermatocytes", "round spermatids", "elongating spermatids"))

To browse the reads of a cell population (e.g. IGV), scalpelR::subsetBAM writes the reads of selected cells (barcodes as in the BAM CB tag, column Barcodes):

rs_barcodes = idge.obj[[]] %>% filter(celltype == "round spermatids", orig.ident == "SRR6129050") %>% pull(Barcodes)
subsetBAM(bam_file = bams[["SRR6129050"]], barcodes = rs_barcodes, output_file = "SRR6129050_round_spermatids.bam", tag = "CB", cores = 4)

3.6 3’ UTR length in single cells

Using the isoform quantification and the genome annotation (3’ UTR of each transcript), scalpelR::weightedUTR_cell computes for each cell the mean over its genes of the weighted 3’ UTR length (isoform usage x isoform 3’ UTR length):

utr3length_tab = weightedUTR_cell(
    seurat_obj = idge.obj,
    annotation_gr = gtf,
    group.by = "celltype") %>%
    mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("spermatocytes", "round spermatids", "elongating spermatids")))
head(utr3length_tab, 5)
                           cells            group wUTRlength.cell n_genes
                          <char>           <fctr>           <num>   <int>
1: SRR6129050_AAACCTGAGCTTATCG-1 round spermatids        314.1385    1121
2: SRR6129050_AAACCTGCATGAGCGA-1 round spermatids        187.5600      25
3: SRR6129050_AAACCTGGTTGAGTTC-1 round spermatids        299.8757     975
4: SRR6129050_AAACCTGTCAACGAAA-1 round spermatids        282.1909    1066
5: SRR6129050_AAACCTGTCAGAAATG-1    spermatocytes        342.5182     110
utr3length_tab %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = group, y = wUTRlength.cell, fill = group)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", trim = T, alpha = .6) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "white", width = .15, outlier.shape = NA) +
    xlab(NULL) + ylab("weighted 3' UTR length (nt)") +
    ggtitle("Average 3' UTR length per cell") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "none")

4 Further downstream analysis

The isoform-based Seurat object can be used as a standard gene-based Seurat object (e.g. trajectory analysis with Monocle3). For more information, see the Seurat documentation.
